name: java
description: Write, build and test Java (Maven/Gradle), Spring Boot or plain JVM. Use for .java files, pom.xml/build.gradle projects and Java build errors.
summary: Idiomatic, well-tested Java built with Maven or Gradle.

name: kotlin
description: Write, build and test Kotlin (JVM/Android/Multiplatform): null-safety, coroutines, data classes. Use for .kt files and Gradle Kotlin projects.
pitfalls: Launching coroutines in the wrong scope (leaks)
Blocking calls on the main dispatcher

name: scala
description: Write and build Scala (sbt) with functional and typed patterns. Use for .scala files and build.sbt projects. Detect sbt/scala before claiming support.
summary: Typed, functional Scala built with sbt.
pitfalls: Overly clever type-level code hurting readability

name: groovy
description: Read and write Groovy, including Gradle build scripts and Jenkins pipelines. Use for .groovy files and Jenkinsfile.
summary: Dynamic JVM scripting for builds and pipelines.
checklist: Secrets from credentials store, not literals
Gradle logic kept declarative where possible
pitfalls: Dynamic typing errors surfacing only at runtime

name: clojure
description: Write and run Clojure/ClojureScript with a REPL-driven workflow and immutable data. Use for .clj/.cljs files and deps.edn/project.clj. Detect clojure/lein first.
summary: REPL-driven, immutable, functional Lisp on the JVM.
checklist: Pure functions; side effects at the edges
REPL used to verify small pieces
pitfalls: Laziness causing side effects at unexpected times

name: swift
description: Write, build and test Swift (SwiftPM, iOS/macOS): optionals, value types, protocols, concurrency. Use for .swift files and Package.swift. Detect swift/xcodebuild first.
summary: Safe, value-oriented Swift with structured concurrency.
checklist: Optionals unwrapped safely (no force unwrap in prod)
Value semantics preferred; reference cycles avoided
pitfalls: Retain cycles from strong self captures

name: objective-c
description: Read, write and maintain Objective-C with ARC and Cocoa patterns. Use for .m/.h Apple sources. Detect clang/xcodebuild first.
pitfalls: Retain cycles capturing self in blocks

name: csharp
description: Write, build and test C# (.NET): async/await, LINQ, nullable reference types. Use for .cs files, .csproj/.sln projects and .NET build errors.
pitfalls: Blocking on async with .Result causing deadlocks

name: fsharp
description: Write and build F# (.NET): immutability, discriminated unions, pattern matching, computation expressions. Use for .fs/.fsx files.
checklist: Domain modeled with DUs; make illegal states unrepresentable

name: vbnet
description: Read and maintain VB.NET (.NET) code. Use for .vb files and legacy .NET projects. Detect dotnet before claiming support.
summary: Maintainable VB.NET interoperating with the .NET ecosystem.
pitfalls: Option Strict Off allowing silent conversions
Legacy On Error Resume Next hiding failures

name: haskell
description: Write and build Haskell (Cabal/Stack): purity, types, type classes, laziness. Use for .hs files and .cabal/stack.yaml. Detect ghc/cabal/stack first.
summary: Pure, strongly typed Haskell with effects at the edges.

name: ocaml
description: Write and build OCaml (Dune/opam): modules, variants, pattern matching. Use for .ml/.mli files and dune-project. Detect ocaml/dune first.
summary: Fast, typed functional OCaml built with Dune.
pitfalls: Mixing mutable refs with functional style carelessly

name: elixir
description: Write, test and build Elixir (Mix, OTP, Phoenix): processes, supervision, immutability. Use for .ex/.exs files and mix.exs. Detect elixir/mix first.
summary: Concurrent, fault-tolerant Elixir on the BEAM.
pitfalls: Doing heavy work in a single process (bottleneck)

name: erlang
description: Write and build Erlang/OTP: actors, supervision, hot code. Use for .erl files and rebar3 projects. Detect erl/rebar3 first.
pitfalls: Blocking a gen_server on long work

name: lisp-scheme
description: Write and run Common Lisp or Scheme (Racket/Guile): macros, recursion, REPL. Use for .lisp/.scm/.rkt files. Detect sbcl/racket/guile first.

name: shell-bash
description: Write robust, portable Bash/POSIX shell scripts with strict mode and shellcheck. Use for .sh files and shell one-liners on POSIX systems.
summary: Safe Bash: strict mode, quoted expansions, shellcheck clean.

name: shell-powershell
description: Write PowerShell (5.1 and 7+) scripts and cmdlets with proper error handling and object pipelines. Use for .ps1/.psm1 files on Windows or cross-platform pwsh.
summary: Object-pipeline PowerShell with real error handling.

name: fish
description: Write Fish shell scripts and functions. Use for .fish files and config.fish. Detect the fish binary before executing.
pitfalls: Copying bash syntax that fish rejects
